2: The Strongest Sage with the Weakest Crest by Shinkoshoto (Square Enix) is a fantasy adventure about a hero starting over on purpose. The greatest sage of his age was born with a crest poorly suited to magic, so he reincarnates far in the future to get a better one. He wakes as young Matthias, only to find that magic has badly declined in his absence. It's a fun, fast read for fans of overpowered heroes and reincarnation stories.
3: Pandora in the Crimson Shell by Masamune Shirow (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted sci-fi action story from the creator of Ghost in the Shell. Nene Nanakorobi, a cheerful girl with a full cyborg body, travels to the island city of Seranos. There she meets Clarion, a gynoid with a prickly attitude, and the two become unlikely partners. Expect cute character moments mixed with cyberpunk tech and action.
5: Faerie's Landing by You Hyun (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy romance with a big dose of comedy. High school student Ryang Jegal's ordinary life changes when Faerie Goodfellow, a fairy exiled from her own world, lands in his. Faerie must live among humans while she works off her punishment, and Ryang gets pulled into the chaos. It's a charming pick for readers who like folklore mixed with school-life humor.
6: Black God by Dall-Young Lim (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series with a touch of romance. Keita Ibuki's life takes a strange turn when he meets Kuro, a powerful girl who guards the balance of the world. Their meeting draws Keita into a hidden struggle tied to people's doppelgangers and the luck they share. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy contract-partner battles and urban fantasy.
7: Rebound by Yuriko Nishiyama (Tokyopop) is a high-energy basketball series and the follow-up to her Harlem Beat. Nate Torres and his teammates at Johnan High chase their dream of winning at the national level. Along the way they face tough rivals, fierce games, and plenty of locker-room comedy. It's a great pick for sports manga fans who love team chemistry and fast-paced court action.
8: High School DxD by Ichiei Ishibumi (Yen Press) is a comedic action fantasy light novel with plenty of fan service. Issei Hyodo, a hopelessly girl-crazy high schooler, finally gets a date, only for her to turn out to be a fallen angel who kills him. He's brought back to life by Rias Gremory, a beautiful upperclassman who is secretly a devil, and becomes her servant. It's for readers who like harem comedy mixed with supernatural battles.
10: Gantz by Hiroya Oku (Dark Horse) is an intense sci-fi action series for mature readers. High schooler Kei Kurono and his old friend Masaru Kato are killed by a subway train. They wake up in an apartment with a mysterious black sphere, along with other people who just died. The sphere sends them out to hunt aliens in a deadly game. It's violent and gripping, made for readers who like survival stories with high stakes.
13: Sensual Phrase by Mayu Shinjo (Viz Media) is a steamy shojo romance set in the music world. High school student Aine Sakurazaka dreams of writing song lyrics. When she meets Sakuya, the lead singer of the hit rock band Lucifer, he takes an interest in both her words and her. Their romance pulls her into the glamorous, complicated world of fame. It's for older teen readers who love dramatic, passionate love stories.
14: Tomb Raider King by San.G (Ize Press) is a Korean action fantasy about a second chance. When mysterious tombs appeared across the world, the relics inside gave people incredible powers. Seo Jooheon spent his life raiding tombs for others, only to be betrayed and killed. Now he's back fifteen years in the past, determined to claim every relic for himself. It's a fast, satisfying read for fans of regression stories and treasure hunting.
16: Battle Vixens by Yuji Shiozaki (Tokyopop) is a martial arts action series with lots of fan service. Its fighters carry magatama beads that bind them to the fates of warriors from China's Three Kingdoms era. Hakufu Sonsaku, a cheerful and powerful fighter, transfers to Nanyo Academy and is quickly drawn into the battles between rival schools. It's for readers who enjoy nonstop brawls and a playful twist on classic history.
19: Sayonara, Football by Naoshi Arakawa (Kodansha) is a heartfelt sports story from the creator of Your Lie in April. Nozomi Onda is a talented soccer player who has always held her own against the boys. Now in middle school, she is told that she can't play in official games with the boys' team. Determined to prove herself, she keeps fighting for a spot on the field. It's an inspiring read for anyone who loves an underdog.
21: Maria Holic by Minari Endou (Tokyopop) is an offbeat school comedy. Kanako Miyamae breaks out in hives whenever a boy touches her, so she transfers to an all-girls Catholic school hoping to find true love. There she meets Mariya Shidou, a stunning student who seems perfect. Kanako soon learns that Mariya is really a sharp-tongued boy in disguise, and she's forced to keep his secret. It's for readers who like snappy, slightly twisted humor.
23: Switch by naked ape (Viz Media) is a gritty crime action series with a mystery at its core. Kai Eto, a sweet-natured rookie, joins a special narcotics unit and is partnered with the sharp, tough Hal Etoh. Together they go undercover to take down drug dealers and the dangerous groups behind them. As the cases grow darker, the partners' own secrets start to surface. It's a good pick for fans of buddy cops and tense drama.
34: Toppu GP by Kosuke Fujishima (Kodansha) is a motorcycle racing story from the creator of Oh My Goddess! Toppu Bando has loved racing since he was a kid and dreams of competing at the very top of the sport. The series follows his rise through the racing world as he faces rivals, setbacks, and the thrill of speed. It's a great fit for readers who enjoy sports stories full of mechanical detail and drive.
38: Reborn as a Space Mercenary by Ryuto (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi adventure light novel. A gamer wakes up inside the world of his favorite space simulation game, along with his powerful starship, the Krishna. Now going by Hiro, he decides to make a living as a mercenary, fighting pirates and taking jobs across the stars. He soon picks up a crew of his own. It's a fun read for fans of isekai with a space-opera twist.
39: Reincarnated as a Dragon Hatchling by Nekoko (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure light novel. After dying, the hero is reborn in a dangerous fantasy world as a newly hatched dragon. He's small, weak, and surrounded by monsters, so he has to fight, level up, and evolve to survive. Along the way he tries to hold on to his human heart. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy monster-reincarnation stories and growth-focused adventures.
41: Freezing by Dall-Young Lim (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi action series with plenty of fan service. Humanity's defenders against the alien Nova are the Pandoras, genetically enhanced young women, and their male partners, the Limiters. Kazuya Aoi arrives at West Genetics Academy and immediately crosses paths with Satellizer el Bridget, a powerful Pandora known as the Untouchable Queen. It's for readers who like intense battles and school rivalries with a dramatic edge.
44: The Hidden Dungeon Only I Can Enter by Meguru Seto (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure with comedy and fan service. Noir Stardia is the son of a low-ranking noble family with few prospects. Everything changes when he stumbles on a secret dungeon that no one else can enter, full of rare treasure and powerful skills. With its help he sets out to get stronger. It's for fans of dungeon-crawling stories and lighthearted harem comedy.
45: The Kingdoms of Ruin by Yoruhashi (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy about revenge. In a world where humans have turned against magic, the witch Chloe is hunted down and killed. Her devoted apprentice, Adonis, survives and vows to make humanity pay. What follows is a bloody, emotional story of grief and vengeance. It's best for readers who like intense, morally gray fantasy with a tragic heart.
51: To Love Ru Darkness by Saki Hasemi (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy with heavy fan service, and the sequel to To Love Ru. Rito Yuki's home is already crowded with alien princesses. Now Momo, one of Lala's younger sisters, has a plan to build Rito a harem, while the assassin Golden Darkness wrestles with her feelings about him. It's for fans of the original who want more chaotic, cheeky comedy.
52: Precarious Woman Executive Miss Black General by Jin (Seven Seas) is a goofy action comedy that pokes fun at superhero shows. The Black General is a top executive in an evil organization that keeps losing to a team of heroes. Her biggest problem? She has fallen for Akagi, the red-suited leader of the heroes she's supposed to be fighting. It's a light, silly read for anyone who enjoys tokusatsu parodies and romantic comedy.
53: Rainbows After Storms by Luka Kobachi (Viz Media) is a sweet yuri romance about two high school girls. Chidori is cool and reserved, while Nijiko is warm and cheerful, and the two are close friends. As they spend more time together, their friendship slowly grows into something more. It's a gentle, heartfelt read for anyone who loves slow-building school romances.
54: Durarara!! by Ryohgo Narita (Yen Press) is an urban fantasy light novel with a big cast and lots of mystery. Mikado Ryugamine moves to Ikebukuro, a lively Tokyo district buzzing with rumors of street gangs, an online group called the Dollars, and a headless rider on a black motorcycle. Soon Mikado learns that some of the rumors are true. It's a great pick for readers who like interwoven stories and quirky characters.
60: Bloody Cross by Shiwo Komeyama (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy action series. Tsukimi is half angel and half vampire, and she carries a curse that will kill her before long. Her only hope is to find a powerful grimoire that might lift it. Along the way, she crosses paths with Hinata, another half-breed with the same curse and his own reasons for wanting the book. It's for fans of supernatural battles and uneasy alliances.
64: Like a Butterfly by Suu Morishita (Viz Media) is a gentle shojo romance. Suiren Shiraishi is so beautiful that people rarely see past her looks, and she is too shy to make real connections. Then she meets Taichi Kawasaki, a quiet, blunt classmate who treats her like anyone else. Slowly the two begin to open up to each other. It's a sweet, low-drama read for fans of soft, slow-burn school romance.
65: Log Horizon: The West Wind Brigade by Koyuki (Yen Press) is a fantasy spin-off of Mamare Touno's Log Horizon. When thousands of players are trapped inside the online game Elder Tale, the skilled samurai Soujirou Seta leads the West Wind Brigade, a guild made up almost entirely of women who adore him. The series follows the guild's adventures and comedy in this new world. It's for Log Horizon fans who want a lighter side story.
66: Sankarea by Mitsuru Hattori (Kodansha) is a quirky romantic comedy with a zombie twist. Chihiro Furuya is a high school boy obsessed with zombie movies who is secretly working on a potion to bring his dead cat back to life. Then he meets Rea Sanka, a sheltered rich girl desperate to escape her overbearing father. When tragedy strikes, Chihiro's potion changes everything. It's a strange, sweet read for fans of offbeat romance.
67: Yakuza Lover by Nozomi Mino (Viz Media) is a dramatic shojo romance for older teens. College student Yuri is saved from an assault by a handsome stranger named Toshiomi Oya. She falls for him at once, only to learn that he is the heir to a powerful yakuza family. As their relationship grows, she's pulled into a dangerous world she never expected. It's for readers who enjoy intense, high-stakes love stories.
68: Lovesick Ellie by Fujimomo (Kodansha) is a funny, sweet shojo romantic comedy. Eleanor Ichimori is a plain, quiet high school girl who secretly posts wild fantasy stories online about the most popular boy in class, Akira Omi. Then Omi discovers her account. Instead of exposing her, he seems oddly interested in her. It's a cute pick for readers who love awkward heroines and a teasing romance.
69: Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D's by Masahiro Hikokubo and Masashi Sato (Viz Media) is a card-battle action series set in the Yu-Gi-Oh! world. In Neo Domino City, duelists face off in Turbo Duels, high-speed card battles fought on motorcycles. Yusei Fudo, a talented young duelist, enters the city's biggest tournament with his own reasons to win. It's a great pick for kids and fans of the anime who love fast-paced card battles.
70: Shortcake Cake by Suu Morishita (Viz Media) is a warm shojo romance set in a boarding house. Ten Nagamori moves into a boarding house so she won't have a long commute to high school. There she lives alongside several classmates, including the charming, outspoken Riku and the quiet, kind Chiaki. As they share daily life, feelings start to grow. It's a gentle, cozy read for fans of slice-of-life romance.
71: Show-ha Shoten! by Akinari Asakura and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a comedy drama about the world of stand-up comedy. Taiyo Azuma is a shy high schooler who secretly writes jokes. Kouta Higashikata is a classmate with a big personality who wants to become a comedian. When the two team up as a comedy duo, they set out to make all of Japan laugh. It's an upbeat read for anyone who loves stories about chasing a dream.
74: Mushoku Tensei: Roxy Gets Serious by Rifujin na Magonote (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure spin-off of Mushoku Tensei. It follows Roxy Migurdia, the young demon-race mage who becomes Rudeus's beloved tutor. The story goes back to her own beginnings as she leaves her village, studies magic, and makes her way as an adventurer. It's a great pick for Mushoku Tensei fans who want to know more about one of its favorite characters.
75: Banished from the Hero's Party, I Decided to Live a Quiet Life in the Countryside by Zappon (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy romance. Red was a member of the Hero's party until he was told he wasn't strong enough and pushed out. Instead of fighting back, he moves to a quiet frontier town to open an apothecary. Then Rit, a famous adventurer he once knew, shows up wanting to live with him. It's a sweet, relaxing read.
77: Kuma Kuma Kuma Bear by Kumanano (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy. Yuna is a fifteen-year-old shut-in who spends her days playing a virtual reality game. One day she wakes up in a fantasy world, wearing a cute bear costume that turns out to be overpowered. Armed with her bear gear, she starts a new life as an adventurer. It's a cheerful, cozy read for anyone who enjoys gentle isekai stories.
78: Me & My Brothers by Hari Tokeino (Tokyopop) is a sweet shojo family comedy. After losing her parents, Sakura is raised by her four older stepbrothers, who all dote on her. As she grows up, she learns more about the family and the bonds that hold them together. It's a heartwarming, lighthearted read for fans of found family and gentle school-life stories.
79: Bungo Stray Dogs: Wan! by Kafka Asagiri and Neco Kanai (Yen Press) is a comedy spin-off of Bungo Stray Dogs. It shrinks the cast of the Armed Detective Agency and the Port Mafia into cute chibi versions. Instead of battles, the series focuses on silly everyday moments and gags. It's a fun, easygoing read for fans of the main series who want to see their favorite characters at play.
80: Plunderer by Suu Minazuki (Yen Press) is a fantasy action series with comedy and fan service. In Hina's world, everyone carries a Count, a number tied to something about their life that can decide their fate. Hina is traveling in search of the legendary Ace, one of the war heroes of the past. Her journey leads her to Licht, a goofy, perverted swordsman with a serious secret. It's for readers who enjoy action with a twist.
81: Farming Life in Another World by Kinosuke Naito (One Peace Books) is a relaxing fantasy slice-of-life story. Hiraku Machio dies after a long illness and is given a second chance in a new world, along with a divine farming tool. He settles in a remote forest and begins clearing land and growing crops. Before long, all kinds of people and creatures come to live with him. It's a calm, cozy pick for fans of village-building stories.
82: Mobile Suit Gundam: The Origin by Yoshikazu Yasuhiko (Vertical) is a sci-fi war drama that retells the original Gundam story. Yasuhiko, the character designer of the first series, revisits the One Year War between the Earth Federation and the Principality of Zeon. Young Amuro Ray climbs into the Gundam and is thrown into battle. The series also digs into the past of Char Aznable. It's a rich read for Gundam fans and lovers of mecha drama.
83: Stepping on Roses by Rinko Ueda (Viz Media) is a historical shojo romance set in Meiji-era Japan. Sumi Kitamura works hard to care for the orphans her brother keeps bringing home, but they're still deep in poverty. Then a wealthy young businessman, Soichiro Ashida, offers to marry her as a business arrangement. Sumi accepts, and must learn to live as a proper lady. It's for readers who love period dramas and contract-marriage romance.
84: Strike the Blood by Gakuto Mikumo (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series. Kojou Akatsuki is a high school student on Itogami Island, a city where demons and humans live side by side. He's also the Fourth Primogenitor, a legendary vampire. Yukina Himeragi, a young sword shaman, is sent to watch him and to stop him if he becomes a threat. It's for fans of vampire action with comedy and romance.
86: For the Kid I Saw in My Dreams by Kei Sanbe (Yen Press) is a dark crime thriller from the creator of Erased. As a boy, Mitsuo Senda lived through a nightmare when his family was attacked and his twin brother was taken. Years later, he's still searching for the people responsible. His hunt pulls him deep into a violent underworld. It's an intense, gripping read for mature fans of revenge stories and mysteries.
87: Full Metal Panic! by Shoji Gatoh (ADV) is an action comedy with mecha and romance. Sousuke Sagara is a teen soldier from the secret mercenary group Mithril. He's sent undercover to a Tokyo high school to protect Kaname Chidori, a girl who may hold dangerous secrets. Sousuke knows everything about war and nothing about normal teenage life, which leads to plenty of chaos. It's great for fans of action mixed with school comedy.
89: Afterschool Charisma by Kumiko Suekane (Viz Media) is a sci-fi mystery set at an unusual school. St. Kleio Academy is home to clones of famous historical figures, including Napoleon, Joan of Arc, and Mozart. Shiro Kamiya, the son of one of the school's teachers, is the only student who isn't a clone. When trouble starts on campus, the school's secrets come to light. It's for readers who like thoughtful sci-fi with a twist.
93: The Beginning After the End by TurtleMe (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure about getting a second shot at life. King Grey ruled a world of great power and strength, but his life was lonely. After his death he's reborn in a world of magic and monsters as Arthur Leywin. With the memories of his old life, he sets out to grow stronger and do things differently this time. It's for fans of reincarnation stories and big fantasy worlds.
94: The Case Files of Jeweler Richard by Nanako Tsujimura (Seven Seas) is a gentle mystery light novel set around a jewelry shop. College student Seigi Nakata meets Richard, a striking British jeweler, while trying to sell an old ring. Seigi takes a part-time job at Richard's shop in Ginza, where every gem seems to come with a story. It's a warm, thoughtful read for fans of character-driven mysteries.
95: The Case Study of Vanitas by Jun Mochizuki (Yen Press) is a gothic fantasy adventure from the creator of Pandora Hearts. In a steampunk version of 19th-century Paris, the young vampire Noé meets Vanitas, a human who says he can cure vampires driven mad by a curse. The two set off together to save vampires and uncover the truth behind it. It's for readers who love stylish art and mysterious, morally gray heroes.
96: The Detective Is Already Dead by Nigozyu (Yen Press) is a mystery light novel with action and comedy. Kimihiko Kimizuka has a knack for getting caught up in trouble. Years ago he was the assistant to Siesta, a brilliant detective, and the two solved cases around the world together. Now Siesta is gone, and Kimihiko is trying to live a normal life, until new trouble finds him. It's for readers who enjoy sharp banter and mysteries.
97: The Drifting Classroom by Kazuo Umezz (Viz Media) is a classic horror survival story. Sho Takamatsu goes to school after a fight with his mom. Without warning, the entire school is transported to a strange, desolate wasteland. With no way home, the students and teachers must struggle to survive as fear and chaos take over. It's a gripping read for fans of vintage horror and survival stories.
98: New Lone Wolf and Cub by Kazuo Koike and Hideki Mori (Dark Horse) is a historical samurai drama and the continuation of Lone Wolf and Cub. Young Daigoro is left alone after the events of the original series. He is taken in by Togo Shigetaka, a master swordsman, and the two set out together on the road. It's a strong choice for fans of samurai tales and the classic original.
99: The Genius Prince's Guide to Raising a Nation Out of Debt by Toru Toba (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel about politics. Prince Wein of the small, struggling kingdom of Natra has to run the country while his father is ill. Wein would love to sell the country off and live a lazy life, but his clever schemes keep turning into successes. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy strategy and scheming heroes.
100: The Great Jahy Will Not Be Defeated! by Wakame Konbu (Square Enix) is a cheerful workplace comedy with a fantasy twist. Jahy was the proud second-in-command of the Dark Realm until a magical girl shattered its mana crystal, leaving her stuck in the human world in a tiny body, and now she rents a cramped apartment and works at a neighborhood bar while plotting her comeback. It's a light, goofy read for anyone who enjoys a fallen villain trying very hard at everyday life.
101: Hell Mode by Hamuo (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure about a gamer who wants a real challenge. Bored with games that are too easy, a hardcore player picks the hardest possible setting and finds himself reborn in another world as Allen, a peasant boy with the rare Summoner class. Leveling up is brutally slow, but he loves the grind. Readers who enjoy careful stat-building and a lead who plans every step will feel right at home.
102: Her Majesty's Dog by Mick Takeuchi (Go! Comi) is a supernatural romance with a gentle, mysterious mood. Amane comes from a remote village and has the power to make her words come true, and she moves to the city for school with Hyoue, a dog spirit who takes human form and serves as her loyal guardian. The pairing of a quiet heroine and her devoted protector makes this a good fit for fans of yokai stories with a romantic thread.
103: Battle Angel Alita: Mars Chronicle by Yukito Kishiro (Kodansha) is a science fiction action series that returns to the world of Battle Angel Alita. This chapter of the saga goes back to Alita's early life on Mars, long before she woke up in the Scrapyard, and follows the events that shaped the girl she became. Kishiro's detailed cyborg designs and hard-hitting fights are all here. Longtime fans will enjoy filling in Alita's past, and it rewards readers who like dense, thoughtful sci-fi.
104: No. 6 by Atsuko Asano (Kodansha) is a science fiction drama set in a city that looks like a perfect utopia. Shion is a gifted boy living a privileged life in No. 6 until, on a stormy night when he is twelve, he shelters a wounded fugitive named Nezumi. That one choice costs him his place in the city and leads him to see what lies beneath its polished surface. It's a moving story about friendship and questioning the world you were raised in.
106: Hikaru no Go by Yumi Hotta (Viz Media) is a coming-of-age story about the ancient board game Go. Sixth grader Hikaru Shindo is poking around his grandfather's attic when he finds an old Go board haunted by Sai, the ghost of a master player from centuries ago. Sai just wants to play again, and Hikaru slowly gets drawn into the game himself. You don't need to know the rules to enjoy it; the rivalries and growth carry the story.
108: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess by Akira Himekawa (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure based on the beloved video game. Link is a quiet young ranch hand in the village of Ordon, carrying scars from his past. When a strange twilight spreads across Hyrule, he is transformed into a wolf and meets Midna, a sharp-tongued imp with her own agenda. This adaptation gives Link a voice and backstory, making it a treat for game fans and newcomers alike.
109: Omamori Himari by Milan Matra (Yen Press) is a supernatural action comedy with plenty of fan service. On his sixteenth birthday, Yuto Amakawa learns that he comes from a family of demon slayers and that the charm protecting him has worn off. Now monsters are after him, and his guardian turns out to be Himari, a cat spirit who fights with a sword. It's a lively harem series for fans of yokai battles mixed with romantic comedy.
111: How Not to Summon a Demon Lord by Yukiya Murasaki (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy comedy with plenty of fan service. Takuma is a shy gamer who plays as the fearsome demon lord Diablo. When he is summoned into a world that looks just like his game, he has his avatar's body and power, but none of the confidence, so he acts like Diablo full-time. Fans of overpowered heroes and awkward social mishaps will have fun with this one.
113: Hyper Police by Minoru Tachikawa (Tokyopop) is a fast, funny action series set in a future where monsters and demi-humans far outnumber humans. Natsuki is a cat-girl bounty hunter working for a small, struggling agency in a rough part of Tokyo. Between rival hunters, dangerous targets, and an empty bank account, every job is a scramble. Readers who enjoy scrappy heroes, quick humor, and creature-filled cityscapes will find a lot to like.
116: I Think I Turned My Childhood Friend into a Girl by Norio Sakurai (Seven Seas) is a light romantic comedy. Itsuki jokingly tells his best friend Mikoto, who has a very pretty face, that he'd look great as a girl. Mikoto takes it to heart and starts showing up to school dressed as one, and Itsuki suddenly can't stop noticing him. It's a sweet, silly story for readers who enjoy cross-dressing comedies and friendships that slowly turn into something more.
117: The Saint's Magic Power Is Omnipotent by Yuka Tachibana (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy romance. Sei is an overworked office worker who is suddenly summoned to another world as its legendary Saint, only to be brushed aside when the prince chooses another girl. Left on her own, she happily takes a job at a research institute making potions, and her work starts turning out far stronger than anyone expected. It's a relaxing read for fans of slow-burn romance and capable heroines.
118: Bloody Monday by Ryou Ryumon (Kodansha) is a high-tension thriller full of hacking and conspiracy. Fujimaru Takagi seems like an ordinary high schooler, but he is secretly a genius hacker who helps his father's government intelligence agency. When a mysterious group plots a terror attack on Tokyo, Fujimaru is pulled into a race against time where anyone could be a traitor. Readers who love twisty spy stories and cyber-thrillers will race through it.
119: I'm the Villainess, So I'm Taming the Final Boss by Sarasa Nagase (Yen Press) is a fantasy romantic comedy. When her prince fiance breaks their engagement in public, Aileen suddenly remembers her past life and realizes she is the villainess of an otome game. Every route ends badly for her, so she comes up with a bold plan: win over Claude, the demon king who is the game's final boss. Fans of clever, determined heroines and villainess stories will enjoy it.
120: Bottom-Tier Character Tomozaki by Yuki Yaku (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy about learning to play the game of life. Fumiya Tomozaki is the top-ranked player of a popular fighting game but a total loner at school, convinced that real life is a broken game. Then he meets his online rival in person and discovers it's Aoi Hinami, the most perfect girl in his class. She decides to coach him, step by step, in a story that's warm, funny, and surprisingly thoughtful.
121: Peach Girl by Miwa Ueda (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance full of high school drama. Momo Adachi has tanned skin and light hair from years on the swim team, so classmates assume she is a party girl, even though she only has eyes for her quiet crush, Toji. Her so-called best friend Sae keeps stirring up trouble, and the flirty Kairi complicates things further. It's a juicy, emotional read for anyone who loves love triangles and frenemy schemes.
122: Im: Great Priest Imhotep by Makoto Morishita (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series with an ancient Egyptian twist. Imhotep, a powerful priest from Egypt's distant past, awakens in modern-day Japan with one mission: to hunt down the Magai, beings that steal the power of the old gods. A local high school girl soon gets swept into his fight. It's a fun mix of mythology, magic battles, and fish-out-of-water humor.
124: Persona 3 by Shuji Sogabe (Udon) is a supernatural action story based on the popular video game. A quiet transfer student arrives at Gekkoukan High and learns that there is a hidden hour between one day and the next, when monsters called Shadows roam. He joins a group of students who fight them by summoning their inner selves, called Personas. Game fans will enjoy seeing the cast come to life, and newcomers get a moody, stylish school adventure.
125: Buso Renkin by Nobuhiro Watsuki (Viz Media) is a shonen action comedy from the creator of Rurouni Kenshin. High schooler Kazuki Muto is killed while trying to save a girl from a monster, but she revives him by replacing his heart with an alchemical core called a kakugane. Now he can summon a weapon of his own and is drawn into a hidden war against man-eating homunculi. It's energetic and big-hearted, with quirky villains and lots of heart.
127: Interviews with Monster Girls by Petos (Kodansha) is a gentle slice-of-life comedy. Tetsuo Takahashi is a high school biology teacher who has always been fascinated by demi-humans, people with traits from folklore. When several students turn out to be a vampire, a dullahan, and a snow woman, he starts listening to what everyday life is like for them. It's kind, funny, and thoughtful, perfect for readers who want a cozy story about understanding others.
128: Inu-Yasha: A Feudal Fairy Tale by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure full of action, humor, and romance. Kagome Higurashi is an ordinary schoolgirl until she is pulled down an old well at her family's shrine and lands in feudal Japan. There she frees Inu-Yasha, a hot-tempered half-demon, and accidentally shatters the magical Shikon Jewel, so now the two must work together to gather the shards. It's a classic for good reason.
129: Candy and Cigarettes by Tomonori Inoue (Seven Seas) is a gritty action thriller. Raizo Shiba is a retired police officer in his sixties who is struggling to support his grandchild, so he takes a job with a secret organization that turns out to be a ring of assassins. His new partner is Miharu, an eleven-year-old girl who is a skilled killer. It's violent and dark, with an odd-couple bond at its center, for readers who enjoy hard-edged crime stories.
130: Captain Harlock: Dimensional Voyage by Leiji Matsumoto (Seven Seas) is a space opera that retells the classic Captain Harlock story. Earth has grown lazy and complacent, and no one is ready for a new threat from beyond the stars. Only the outlaw Harlock and the crew of his ship, the Arcadia, are willing to fight, and young Tadashi Daiba joins them after losing his father. It's a stirring, old-school adventure for sci-fi fans and newcomers to Matsumoto's universe.
131: Though I Am an Inept Villainess by Satsuki Nakamura (Seven Seas) is a palace fantasy comedy with a body-swap twist. Kou Reirin is the most beloved consort candidate in the imperial court, while Shu Keigetsu is the most despised. Keigetsu uses forbidden magic to switch bodies with Reirin, expecting her rival to fall apart, but instead the cheerful Reirin is delighted with her healthy new body. It's sweet, clever, and full of court intrigue and close friendship between women.
132: Threads of Time by Mi Young Noh (Tokyopop) is a historical fantasy set during the Mongol invasions of Korea. Moon Bin is a modern teenage boy who keeps having strange dreams about life in the thirteenth century. After an accident, he wakes up living that life as the son of a Korean noble, caught in a time of war. It's a sweeping story of friendship, loyalty, and danger for readers who enjoy history mixed with adventure.
134: Kagetora by Akira Segami (Del Rey) is a romantic comedy with ninja action. Kagetora is a skilled young ninja sent to serve and protect Yuki, the heir of a respected martial arts family. The trouble is that Yuki is clumsy, gentle, and hopeless at fighting, and she wants him to teach her ninja skills, while he tries very hard not to fall for her. Fans of sweet romance and lighthearted action will enjoy it.
135: Clockwork Planet by Yuu Kamiya (Kodansha) is a science fiction adventure set on an Earth rebuilt entirely out of gears. High schooler Naoto Miura is an outcast who loves machines more than anything. One day a coffin crashes through his roof, holding a broken automaton named RyuZU, and repairing her pulls him into a plot that could decide the fate of the planet. Its steampunk world is a delight for fans of mechanical fantasy.
136: Psychic Academy by Katsu Aki (Tokyopop) is a science fiction school story in a world where psychic powers are common. Ai Shiomi is the younger brother of a famous hero, but his own abilities are weak, and he enrolls at a special academy for psychics feeling the pressure of his brother's name. There he struggles with his studies, his powers, and his feelings for two very different girls. It's a mix of romance, growing up, and psychic battles.
137: Toradora! by Yuyuko Takemiya (Seven Seas) is a high school romantic comedy. Ryuji Takasu is a kind, tidy boy whose sharp eyes make everyone think he's a delinquent, while Taiga Aisaka is tiny but has a fierce temper that's earned her the nickname "Palmtop Tiger." When they discover each has a crush on the other's best friend, they team up to help each other. It's funny and heartfelt, with a cast that feels like real teenagers.
138: Trillion Game by Riichiro Inagaki (Viz Media) is a business drama with a gambler's swagger. Haru is a smooth-talking risk-taker who can charm anyone, and Gaku is a shy computer genius who can build anything. The two old friends make a wild promise to earn a trillion dollars together, starting with almost nothing, and the bluffing is half the fun. It's great for readers who like underdog schemes and fast-paced strategy.
139: Kakuriyo: Bed & Breakfast for Spirits by Waco Ioka (Viz Media) is a cozy fantasy romance with lots of good food. Aoi Tsubaki inherited her grandfather's ability to see spirits, and also, it turns out, his debt. An ogre carries her off to the spirit world and tells her she must marry him to settle it, but Aoi refuses and decides to work off the debt herself by cooking for spirits. It's a warm, charming read for fans of yokai stories.
142: Reborn as a Space Mercenary by Shinichi Matsui (Seven Seas) is a science fiction adventure with a gamer's spirit. A man who loved playing a space simulation game wakes up inside its world, along with his powerful ship. With nothing else to rely on, he decides to make a living as a mercenary, picking up jobs, fighting pirates, and gaining unlikely companions along the way. It's a fun, easygoing read for fans of spaceship battles and isekai adventures.
143: Ubel Blatt by Etorouji Shiono (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy revenge story. Years ago, seven heroes were sent to stop an invading army, but three of them were betrayed and killed by their own companions, who then took the credit. Now a mysterious young swordsman named Koinzell sets out to hunt down the false heroes who rule the land. It's violent and mature, with striking art, for readers who enjoy grim fantasy and stories of vengeance.
144: Vampire Hunter D by Hideyuki Kikuchi (DMP) is a gothic horror adventure based on the classic novels. Far in the future, the world is a wasteland ruled by vampire aristocrats called Nobles, and humans live in fear. D is a quiet, half-human, half-vampire hunter who travels from town to town taking jobs to destroy them, drawn here in dark, moody art. It's a great pick for fans of vampire stories and post-apocalyptic westerns.
145: Kitchen Princess by Miyuki Kobayashi (Kodansha) is a sweet shojo romance about cooking. Najika is an orphan with an incredible sense of taste and a big heart. Years ago, a boy comforted her with a dish of flan, and she has been looking for her "flan prince" ever since, and her search leads her to an elite academy, where her cooking wins friends and makes rivals. It's heartwarming and full of food, with a dash of drama.
147: Rosario + Vampire by Akihisa Ikeda (Viz Media) is a supernatural comedy with lots of action. Tsukune Aono is an average guy who accidentally enrolls at Yokai Academy, a school for monsters where humans are not allowed. On his first day he meets Moka Akashiya, a sweet girl who turns out to be a vampire, and now he has to keep his secret and survive. It's a fun mix of harem comedy and monster battles.
148: Descendants of Darkness by Yoko Matsushita (Viz Media) is a supernatural mystery series. Asato Tsuzuki works for the Ministry of Hades as a shinigami, an agent of death who guides souls that won't move on. He is cheerful and easygoing on the surface, and paired with a prickly new partner, Hisoka Kurosaki, who has his own dark past, to investigate strange deaths. It's moody, emotional, and stylish, for readers who like detective stories with a gothic edge.
149: Let This Grieving Soul Retire by Rai Hebino (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy built on misunderstandings. Krai Andrey leads one of the most famous treasure-hunting parties in the land, and everyone believes he is a brilliant mastermind. In truth, he is weak, timid, and would love nothing more than to quit, yet every offhand remark he makes gets taken as a stroke of genius. It's a fun read for fans of accidental heroes and gentle humor.
150: Level 1 Demon Lord and One Room Hero by Toufu (Seven Seas) is a relaxed fantasy comedy. Years after being defeated, the Demon Lord is revived at level one and sets out to find the hero who beat him. He finds him living in a tiny apartment, unemployed and playing video games all day, so with nowhere else to go, the Demon Lord moves in and starts keeping house. It's a cozy, funny slice of life for fans of fantasy parody.
151: Do You Love Your Mom and Her Two-Hit Multi-Target Attacks? by Dachima Inaka (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy with a twist on the isekai formula. High schooler Masato Oosuki is chosen to test a new game that sends players into a fantasy world. He dreams of becoming a hero, but his mother, Mamako, comes along too and turns out to be far stronger than he is. It's a silly, good-natured story about family that pokes fun at gaming tropes.
152: Sasaki and Peeps by Buncololi (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy about a middle-aged office worker who stumbles into adventure. Sasaki buys a little sparrow to keep him company, and the bird turns out to be Peeps, a great sage from another world. Peeps lets Sasaki travel back and forth between Earth and that world, where he starts a side business, though he soon gets drawn into strange events at home too. It's laid-back and genre-bending.
155: Magical Explorer by Iris (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure with a gamer's twist. A man who knew his favorite fantasy game inside and out wakes up reborn as Kousuke Takioto, a minor side character whose job is just to support the hero. Using everything he remembers about the game, he decides to become as strong as possible on his own terms. It's a fun read for fans of game-world stories and clever strategy.
156: Maid Sama! by Hiro Fujiwara (Tokyopop) is a shojo romantic comedy. Misaki Ayuzawa is the tough student council president at a school that used to be all boys, but she has a secret: to help her family, she works part-time at a maid cafe, and when the popular, carefree Takumi Usui finds out, he keeps her secret and keeps showing up. It's funny, charming, and full of heart.
159: Emma by Kaoru Mori (CMX) is a gentle historical romance set in Victorian London. Emma is a quiet, hardworking maid who catches the eye of William Jones, the eldest son of a wealthy merchant family. Their feelings for each other grow, but the class divide between them is hard to ignore. Mori's detailed art brings the era to life, making this a lovely pick for fans of slow romance and period drama.
161: Fate/stay night by Type-Moon (Tokyopop) is an action fantasy based on the hit visual novel. Shirou Emiya is a high schooler with a bit of magic training and a strong sense of justice. One night he stumbles into the Holy Grail War, a secret battle between mages and the legendary heroes they summon. Near death, he summons a hero of his own, the knight Saber, in a story full of intense magic battles.
162: Shibuya Goldfish by Hiroumi Aoi (Yen Press) is a survival horror thriller. One day, Tokyo's busy Shibuya district is suddenly sealed off from the outside world, and giant man-eating goldfish begin swimming through the air. A high school boy trapped inside must find a way to protect the people he cares about and figure out what is happening before they are all eaten. It's tense and strange, for readers who enjoy monster panic stories.
165: Are You Alice? by Ikumi Katagiri (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy mystery inspired by Alice in Wonderland. A young man with no memory of his past suddenly finds himself in Wonderland, where he is given the name Alice and a single command: kill the White Rabbit, while the Mad Hatter, the Cheshire Cat, and other familiar faces all seem to know more than they say. It's a stylish, twisty retelling for fans of unusual takes on classic stories.
166: Kakuriyo: Bed & Breakfast for Spirits by Waco Ioka (Viz Media) is a cozy fantasy romance with lots of good food. Aoi Tsubaki inherited her grandfather's ability to see spirits, and also, it turns out, his debt. An ogre carries her off to the spirit world and tells her she must marry him to settle it, but Aoi refuses and decides to work off the debt herself by cooking for spirits. It's a warm, charming read for fans of yokai stories.
167: Please Go Home, Miss Akutsu! by Yuu Nagira (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Ooyama is a quiet high school boy who just wants to spend his free time at home. For some reason, Akutsu, a tough-looking girl from his school, keeps showing up at his house and making herself comfortable, though she is clearly flustered around him. It's a light, teasing story for fans of slow-burn romance.
169: Iron Wok Jan! by Shinji Saijyo (Comics One) is a cooking battle series full of attitude. Jan Akiyama was trained in Chinese cooking by his legendary chef grandfather, and he is brilliant and very cocky about it. When he takes a job at a famous Tokyo restaurant, he clashes with the owner's granddaughter Kiriko, a talented chef in her own right. It's loud, competitive, and full of mouthwatering dishes for fans of food manga.
170: Inu x Boku SS by Cocoa Fujiwara (Yen Press) is a supernatural romantic comedy. Ririchiyo Shirakiin comes from a powerful family and has a sharp tongue she can't seem to control. Hoping to live on her own, she moves into an exclusive apartment building where every resident gets a personal Secret Service agent, and hers is Soushi Miketsukami, a devoted young man who is also a fox spirit. It's sweet, quirky, and full of colorful yokai residents.
171: The Most Heretical Last Boss Queen by Tenichi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy story about rewriting your fate. At eight years old, Princess Pride Royal Ivy remembers her past life and realizes she is the cruel villain and final boss of an otome game. In the game, she grows up to ruin countless lives, including her own, so she sets out to become a kind and worthy queen instead. It's heartfelt and earnest.
172: Konohana Kitan by Sakuya Amano (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy slice of life. Yuzu is a cheerful young fox girl who has just started working at Konohanatei, an inn for spirits and gods. She is eager to learn, but everything is new, and each chapter brings a new guest and a small, warm story. It's soothing and pretty, a good pick for readers who want something calm and kind.
173: My Quiet Blacksmith Life in Another World by Tamamaru (J-Novel Club) is a relaxing fantasy slice of life. After dying in an accident, a man is reborn in another world as Eizo, with a gift for crafting and blacksmithing. Wanting a peaceful life, he builds a forge deep in a forest that most people avoid, where a few unexpected visitors soon become companions. It's a calm, cozy read for fans of crafting, home life, and found family.
174: Tune by Derek Kirk Kim (First Second) is a funny, offbeat science fiction graphic novel. Andy Go is a young art school dropout who needs a job and has no idea what to do with his life. Then he gets an unusual offer: live as an exhibit in an alien zoo in a parallel universe, in exchange for a good paycheck. It's sharp, awkward, and very relatable, for readers who enjoy humor about growing up.
175: The Executioner and Her Way of Life by Mato Sato (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy adventure. In a world where people from Japan are sometimes summoned with dangerous powers, Menou works in secret as an executioner whose job is to kill them. Her newest target is Akari, a cheerful girl who seems impossible to kill, so Menou travels with her while she looks for a way. It's an intense, emotional story about duty and an unlikely bond.
176: A Business Proposal by Narak (Ize Press) is a lively office romantic comedy based on a popular webtoon. Shin Ha-ri agrees to go on a blind date in her friend's place, planning to act so badly that the man will leave. The problem is that her date turns out to be Kang Tae-mu, the CEO of her own company, and he wants to marry her. It's funny and sweet, perfect for fans of K-dramas and fake-dating stories.
178: Sunshine Sketch by Ume Aoki (Yen Press) is a gentle slice-of-life comedy. Yuno has just started at an art high school and moves into the Hidamari Apartments, right across the street. Her neighbors are fellow art students, and together they share meals, worry about assignments, and enjoy the small moments of everyday life. It's relaxing, warm, and funny, perfect for anyone who wants a calm, cozy read.
181: After School Nightmare by Setona Mizushiro (Go! Comi) is a psychological drama with a supernatural edge. Mashiro Ichijo is a high school student who lives as a boy while hiding a secret about his body, and he is placed in a mysterious class that meets only in dreams, where students battle each other in shared nightmares to earn their graduation. It's unsettling and thought-provoking, for readers who like stories about identity, fear, and growing up.
182: Sword Art Online Progressive by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action series that retells the story of Sword Art Online from the very beginning. Thousands of players are trapped inside a virtual reality game where dying in the game means dying in real life. This version follows Kirito and Asuna as they fight their way through Aincrad one floor at a time, starting on the first. It fills in many details fans have long wanted to see.
183: Tactics by Sakura Kinoshita (ADV) is a supernatural comedy set in early twentieth-century Japan. Kantaro Ichinomiya is a folklorist who can see yokai and spirits. He frees a powerful tengu named Haruka, who becomes his companion, and the two take on jobs exorcising troublesome spirits while Kantaro looks for answers about his past. It's playful and charming, for fans of yokai stories with a sense of humor.
184: Akame ga Kill! Zero by Takahiro and Kei Toru (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy action prequel to Akame ga Kill! Long before she joined Night Raid, Akame was sold as a child along with her sister and trained to become an elite assassin for the Empire. It's violent and gripping, a strong pick for fans of the original who want to see Akame's past.
185: Genshiken by Kio Shimoku (Del Rey) is a comedy about otaku culture. College freshman Kanji Sasahara is a secret anime and manga fan who finally finds his people when he joins the Society for the Study of Modern Visual Culture. The club spends its time playing games, arguing about anime, and making comics, even after a non-fan starts tagging along with her boyfriend. It's funny and honest, for anyone who has ever been a fan.
187: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation by Rifujin na Magonote (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure that helped shape the isekai genre. A thirty-four-year-old shut-in who wasted his life dies in an accident and is reborn in a world of magic as Rudeus Greyrat, with all his memories intact. Determined to live properly this time, he starts training in magic as a small child. It's a sprawling story of growth and second chances.
188: Alice 19th by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy romance. Alice Seno is a shy girl who lives in the shadow of her popular older sister. One day she saves a strange rabbit from a car, and it gives her the ability to use Lotis Words, magical words that can reach the hearts of others, and soon she must learn to use them. It's sweet and dramatic, from the creator of Fushigi Yugi.
189: Alice and Zoroku by Tetsuya Imai (Seven Seas) is a heartwarming fantasy slice of life. Sana is a young girl with an unusual power called the Dreams of Alice, which lets her turn her imagination into reality. After escaping from a research facility, she meets Zoroku, a grumpy old florist who takes her in, and their unlikely bond is the heart of the story. It's charming and kind, with just enough action to keep things exciting.
190: Tenjho Tenge by Oh! Great (CMX) is a martial arts action series with lots of fan service. Souichiro Nagi and his friend Bob Makihara transfer to Toudou Academy, planning to take over the school. Instead, they run straight into the Juken Club, a group of skilled fighters who have their own reasons for battling the school's powerful Executive Council. Its intense, beautifully drawn fights make it a good pick for readers who like gritty action.
191: Girls Bravo by Mario Kaneda (Tokyopop) is a fan service-heavy romantic comedy. Yukinari Sasaki is a timid boy with a strange problem: he breaks out in hives whenever a girl touches him. One day he falls into another world called Seiren, where women far outnumber men, and meets Miharu, a cheerful girl whose touch doesn't make him break out. It's silly and lighthearted, for fans of harem comedies.
192: The Angel Next Door Spoils Me Rotten by Saekisan (Yen Press) is a gentle romance about two neighbors. Amane Fujimiya is a lazy high schooler who lives alone, and Mahiru Shiina is the most admired girl at school, known as an angel, and she happens to live next door. After Amane lends her his umbrella on a rainy day, she starts cooking for him. It's slow and cozy, for readers who love sweet romance.
193: Anne Happy by Cotoji (Yen Press) is a cute school comedy. Ann Hanakoizumi is so unlucky that she gets hit by everything from flying birds to falling trees. She and a group of other girls with similarly hopeless luck are placed in a special class meant to teach them how to be happy. It's silly, sweet, and upbeat, for fans of cheerful slice-of-life stories.
194: The Disappearance of Nagato Yuki-chan by Nagaru Tanigawa (Yen Press) is a gentle romantic comedy set in an alternate version of the Haruhi Suzumiya world. Here Yuki Nagato is not an alien, but a shy, ordinary girl who runs the school literature club. She has a crush on Kyon, the boy who just joined. It's a sweet, low-key spin-off for longtime Haruhi fans and newcomers alike.
197: Happy Sugar Life by Tomiyaki Kagisora (Yen Press) is a dark psychological horror story. Satou Matsuzaka is a popular high school girl who has never understood love, until she meets Shio, a little girl she takes home to live with her. Satou is determined to protect the life they share in her apartment, and she is willing to do anything at all to keep it secret. It's disturbing and gripping, for readers who like unsettling stories.
198: Harukana Receive by Nyoijizai (Seven Seas) is a sports slice of life about beach volleyball. Haruka Ozora moves from Tokyo to Okinawa to live with her grandmother and her cousin Kanata, who used to play beach volleyball but quit, and Haruka's enthusiasm draws her back to the sand as partners. It's upbeat, fun, and full of summer energy, perfect for fans of friendship and sports stories.
200: The Girl I Saved on the Train Turned Out to Be My Childhood Friend by Kennoji (Yen Press) is a sweet romantic comedy. On his morning train, a high school boy steps in to protect a girl from a groper, then thinks nothing more of it. The girl turns out to be his childhood friend, back in town and grown into the most popular girl at school, and she has never stopped caring about him. It's a gentle, cozy read for fans of slow-burn school romance.
201: The Greatest Demon Lord Reborn as a Typical Nobody by Myojin Katou (Yen Press) is a fantasy action comedy. The Demon Lord Varvatos, tired of being feared and alone, reincarnates thousands of years later hoping for an ordinary life with real friends. He's reborn as Ard Meteor, only to find that magic has declined so far that his everyday abilities are now considered impossible. It's a lighthearted overpowered-hero story for readers who enjoy academy life and big misunderstandings.
202: High School Prodigies Have It Easy in Another World by Riku Misora (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Seven of Japan's most gifted teenagers, including a politician, a doctor, an inventor, and a magician, survive a plane crash and wake up in a medieval fantasy world. Using their modern skills, they set out to change the kingdom that takes them in. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy clever problem-solving and modern know-how in another world.
204: Beauty Pop by Kiyoko Arai (Viz Media) is a lively shojo comedy about hair, style, and rivalry. Kiri Koshiba is a sleepy, offhand girl who happens to be a brilliant hairstylist, though she'd rather nobody knew. Her talent puts her in the sights of the Scissors Project, a group of school heartthrobs who give makeovers, and especially their proud leader, Narumi. It's a bright, funny read for fans of makeover stories and bickering romance.
205: The Magic in This Other World is Too Far Behind! by Gamei Hitsuji (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy action story. Suimei Yakagi is pulled into another world along with his friend, who has been summoned as the hero. Suimei is secretly a modern-day magician, and he quickly finds that his magic, built on real science and study, is far beyond anything this world knows. He just wants to find a way home. It suits readers who enjoy detailed magic systems and a capable, low-key lead.
206: The Mortal Instruments by Cassandra Clare (Yen Press) is a manga-style adaptation of the urban fantasy novels. Fifteen-year-old Clary Fray is at a New York nightclub when she witnesses a murder that no one else can see, committed by teenagers covered in strange tattoos. They are Shadowhunters, warriors who hunt demons, and Clary is about to learn she is part of their hidden world. It's a good fit for fans of the books or readers new to urban fantasy romance.
207: The Record of a Fallen Vampire by Kyo Shirodaira (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy action series. Akabara Strauss, the King of Vampires, has spent a thousand years searching for a way to bring back his queen, Stella. Humans and dhampirs alike hunt him, and his quest pulls in old enemies and uneasy allies. It's a moody, dramatic read for fans of vampire stories with sweeping, tragic love at their heart.
208: I Cannot Reach You by Mika (Yen Press) is a tender boys' love romance. Yamato has been in love with his childhood best friend, Kakeru, for years, but he's sure Kakeru only sees him as a friend. Keeping his feelings quiet gets harder as the two grow up and the people around them start pairing off. It's a gentle, heartfelt story for readers who enjoy slow-burn friends-to-lovers romance.
209: Othello by Satomi Ikezawa (Kodansha) is a shojo drama about a girl with two very different sides. Yaya Higuchi is shy and easily pushed around by her classmates, but she has a bold, fearless alternate personality named Nana who comes out when Yaya can't stand up for herself. Yaya doesn't know Nana exists, which leads to plenty of trouble. It's an engaging read for fans of school drama and stories about finding your own voice.
210: I Kept Pressing the 100-Million-Year Button and Came Out on Top by Syuichi Tsukishima (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Allen Rodol is a swordsman with no talent at all, mocked at his academy. Then he finds a strange button that traps him alone in a void for a hundred million years, and he decides to spend all of that time training. He keeps pressing it again and again. It's a satisfying underdog story for readers who love hard work paying off.
211: I Shall Survive Using Potions! by FUNA (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy comedy. After an accidental death, Kaoru Nagase is reborn in another world with one special power: she can create any potion she can imagine, in whatever container she likes. Determined to live quietly and comfortably, she sets out to make her way using her unusual gift. It's a light, fun read for fans of clever, practical heroines and easygoing isekai adventures.
213: Bloody Mary by Akaza Samamiya (Viz Media) is a supernatural shojo story with a dark edge. Bloody Mary is a vampire who has lived for centuries and wants only to die, but nothing can kill him. He believes the young priest Maria Ichiro can, but Maria refuses. Maria has his own problem: he is being hunted, so the two strike a deal, with Mary acting as his bodyguard. It suits fans of moody vampire tales and prickly partnerships.
214: Peach Girl: Change of Heart by Miwa Ueda (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance drama that continues the story of Peach Girl. Momo Adachi's sun-tanned look has always gotten her labeled a party girl, even though she's honest and sweet. Her love life stays complicated, thanks to the two boys she's torn between and a scheming "friend" who never stops making trouble. It's a classic for readers who love high school romance full of twists.
215: Ikigami: The Ultimate Limit by Motoro Mase (Viz Media) is a seinen psychological drama. In a society that claims to teach the value of life, a small number of young adults are chosen at random to die, and they get just 24 hours of warning. Kengo Fujimoto is a government worker whose job is to deliver those death notices. Each story follows one person's final day. It's a thoughtful, often moving read for fans of dystopian drama.
216: Pet Shop of Horrors by Matsuri Akino (Tokyopop) is a supernatural horror series told in short stories. In Los Angeles's Chinatown, the mysterious Count D runs a pet shop that sells rare and wondrous animals, each with a contract that must be obeyed. When customers break the rules, terrible things follow, and Detective Leon Orcot is determined to prove D is behind it. It's an eerie, stylish read for fans of moral fables and dark mystery.
217: Bunny Drop by Yumi Unita (Yen Press) is a warm slice-of-life drama. Daikichi, a thirty-year-old single office worker, goes to his grandfather's funeral and learns the old man left behind a six-year-old daughter, Rin, whom no one in the family wants to take. On impulse, Daikichi offers to raise her himself. It's a gentle, often funny look at learning to be a parent, perfect for readers who enjoy found-family stories.
220: The Witch and the Beast by Kousuke Satake (Kodansha) is a dark fantasy action series. Guideau is a fierce young woman with fangs and a beast's temper, the result of a witch's curse. She travels with Ashaf, a polite, smiling man who carries a coffin, as they track down witches and the trouble they cause. It's a stylish, gothic read for fans of monster hunting, sharp action, and mismatched partners.
221: Inuyashiki by Hiroya Oku (Kodansha) is a seinen sci-fi action story. Ichiro Inuyashiki is an aging office worker whose family ignores him, until an alien accident kills him and rebuilds him as an incredibly powerful machine. He decides to use his new body to help people. A teenage boy changed in the same accident makes a very different choice. It's a tense, emotional read for fans of unusual superhero stories.
222: Ishura by Keiso (Yen Press) is a seinen fantasy action series. The True Demon King, who brought the world to the edge of ruin, is dead, but no one knows who killed him. Now a crowd of monstrously powerful warriors, each a legend in their own right, step forward to fight for the title of true hero. It's a big, bold story for readers who love powerful fighters and dramatic duels.
223: Itazura Na Kiss by Kaoru Tada (DMP) is a classic shojo romantic comedy. Kotoko Aihara, a cheerful but not-so-bright student, finally confesses to Naoki Irie, the school's cold genius, and he turns her down flat. Then an earthquake destroys her house, and she and her father move in with an old family friend, who turns out to be Naoki's father. It's a funny, beloved story for readers who enjoy opposites-attract romance.
224: Tiger & Bunny by Mizuki Sakakibara (Viz Media) is a superhero action comedy based on the anime. In Sternbild City, superheroes fight crime on a live TV show, wearing their sponsors' logos. Veteran hero Kotetsu, known as Wild Tiger, is old-fashioned and past his peak, and he's forced to team up with Barnaby Brooks Jr., a cool, ambitious rookie. It's a fun buddy story for fans of heroes and odd-couple partnerships.
226: Tokyo Mew Mew by Reiko Yoshida and Mia Ikumi (Tokyopop) is a magical girl adventure. While on a date, Ichigo Momomiya is caught in a strange event that merges her DNA with an endangered wildcat. Soon she can transform into a cat-eared superheroine, and she has to find other girls like her to fight aliens who threaten the Earth. It's a cute, upbeat read for magical girl fans of all ages.
227: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Adventure! by Shigekatsu Ihara (Viz Media) is a kids' adventure comedy. Hareta is an energetic boy who grew up in the wilderness, and he sets out to become a Pokémon Trainer with his partner, Piplup. Along the way he meets new friends and rivals in the Sinnoh region and gets caught up in a mystery involving the legendary Pokémon. It's a lively, easy read for young Pokémon fans.
228: Citrus by Saburouta (Seven Seas) is a yuri romance drama. Yuzu Aihara is a stylish, outgoing girl who transfers to a strict all-girls school after her mother remarries. On her first day, she clashes with Mei, the cold and beautiful student council president, only to learn that Mei is her new stepsister. It's an intense, dramatic romance for readers who like their love stories full of tension.
229: Toradora! by Yuyuko Takemiya (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy light novel. Ryuji Takasu is a kind boy with a scary face that makes everyone think he's a delinquent. Taiga Aisaka is tiny, fierce, and known as the "Palmtop Tiger." When the two discover that each has a crush on the other's best friend, they team up to help each other. It's a funny, heartfelt story for fans of school romance.
230: Usotoki Rhetoric by Ritsu Miyako (One Peace Books) is a historical mystery. In early twentieth-century Japan, Kanoko Urabe has the ability to tell when someone is lying, a gift that has made her life lonely. Arriving in the city with nowhere to go, she meets Iwai, a broke young detective who sees how useful her talent could be. It's a charming read for fans of period settings and cozy detective stories.
231: Kiss and White Lily for My Dearest Girl by Canno (Yen Press) is a yuri romance. Ayaka Shiramine works harder than anyone at her school to be the best, yet she can never beat Yurine Kurosawa, a carefree genius who barely seems to try. The two rivals start to see each other in a new light. It's a sweet, gentle series that also follows other girls at the school, great for readers who enjoy soft school romance.
232: Remote by Seimaru Amagi (Tokyopop) is a seinen mystery thriller. Kurumi Ayaki is a cheerful traffic cop who is suddenly assigned to a special unit for unusual crimes. Her new boss, Inspector Himuro, never leaves his basement, so Kurumi becomes his eyes and ears in the field, following his orders by phone. It's a gripping, case-based read for fans of police procedurals.
233: RG Veda by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a sweeping fantasy adventure. Three hundred years after the warlord Taishakuten seized the throne of Heaven, the warrior Yasha-o is entrusted with a child from a fallen clan, Ashura. A prophecy says six stars will gather to change the heavens, and Yasha-o sets out to find them. It's a dramatic, beautifully drawn early CLAMP work for fans of myth-inspired fantasy.
234: Roll Over and Die by Kiki (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy drama. Flum Apricot is chosen by the gods to join the hero's party, but her stats are all zero, and her companions see her as dead weight. Betrayed and sold into slavery, she finds a cursed weapon that turns her weakness into strength. It's a tough, emotional read with a lot of heart, suited to older readers who like underdog stories.
235: Sabikui Bisco by Shinji Cobkubo (Yen Press) is a sci-fi adventure set in a rust-blighted Japan. A deadly Rust Wind is eating away the land, and Bisco Akaboshi, a wanted archer whose arrows grow mushrooms, is searching for a legendary cure. He crosses paths with Milo, a gentle young doctor, and the two set out on a wild journey together. It's a colorful, energetic read for fans of buddy adventures.
237: Wild Ones by Kiyo Fujiwara (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy. After her mother dies, Sachie Wakamura goes to live with the grandfather she's never met, and discovers he's the head of a yakuza family. Her new home is full of tough guys, including Rakuto, the handsome young man assigned as her bodyguard. It's a funny, sweet romance for readers who enjoy an ordinary girl in an extraordinary household.
240: Lord Marksman and Vanadis by Tsukasa Kawaguchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy war story. Tigrevurmud Vorn, called Tigre, is a young earl and a brilliant archer in a kingdom that looks down on the bow. When his side loses a battle, he's taken prisoner by Eleonora Viltaria, one of the powerful warrior women known as Vanadis. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy battles, strategy, and a bit of romance.
242: Yashahime: Princess Half-Demon by Takashi Shiina (Viz Media) is a fantasy action sequel to Inuyasha. Towa and Setsuna are twin half-demon daughters of Sesshomaru, separated as children when Towa is thrown into modern-day Japan. Years later the sisters meet again, along with Moroha, the daughter of Inuyasha and Kagome. It's an exciting adventure for longtime Inuyasha fans and new readers alike.
243: Dragon Goes House-Hunting by Kawo Tanuki (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Letty is a dragon, but he's timid, weak, and kicked out of his family's nest. He just wants a safe place to live, so he teams up with Dearia, a powerful elf who happens to be a real estate agent. Together they tour castles, caves, and dungeons looking for the perfect home. It's a gentle, funny read for anyone who likes cozy fantasy.
245: Dreamin' Sun by Ichigo Takano (Seven Seas) is a shojo romance. Shimana Kameko has run away from home after feeling unwanted by her family. She meets a stranger who offers her a room in his house on one condition: she must tell him her dream. Shimana moves in with an unusual group of housemates and starts to find her place. It's a warm, quirky romance for readers who enjoy found-family stories.
246: Young Ladies Don't Play Fighting Games by Eri Ejima (Seven Seas) is a comedy. At an elite academy for young ladies, Ayaka Shiratori is supposed to be a model of grace and good manners, but she secretly loves fighting games. When she discovers a classmate who shares her passion, their matches get very competitive. It's a fun, silly read for gamers and fans of high-society comedy.
248: Mayo Chiki! by Hajime Asano (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Kinjiro Sakamachi has a problem: being around girls gives him nosebleeds. Then he stumbles on a secret about Subaru Konoe, the handsome and popular butler of the school's richest girl: Subaru is actually a girl. To keep her job, Subaru needs Kinjiro to stay quiet. It's a lighthearted read for fans of school comedies and secret-identity romance.
249: Shimazaki in the Land of Peace by Gouten Hamada (Vertical) is a seinen action drama. Shimazaki was taken as a child and raised as a soldier for an international terrorist group. Now he's living in Japan, trying to build a quiet, ordinary life. His past is never far behind him. It's a tense, thoughtful read for fans of action stories about violence and second chances.
251: Skeleton Knight in Another World by Ennki Hakari (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure. A gamer falls asleep and wakes up in the body of his game character, a heavily armored knight, only to find that under the armor he's a skeleton. Calling himself Arc, he sets out to live peacefully and help people along the way. It's a fun, easygoing story for readers who like a strong, good-hearted lead.
252: Snowball Earth by Yuhiro Tsujitsugu (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action story. Tetsuo is a shy young pilot who, with his giant robot partner Yukio, fought a desperate battle to protect Earth from alien invaders. After the fight, Tetsuo wakes from a long sleep to find the planet covered in ice and his world changed. It's a gripping series for fans of mecha and survival stories.
254: Chitose Is in the Ramune Bottle by Hiromu (Yen Press) is a school romance drama. Saku Chitose is at the top of his high school's social ladder: handsome, popular, and surrounded by friends. His teacher asks him to help a shut-in classmate who has stopped coming to school. It's a thoughtful youth story for readers who enjoy high school life, friendships, and plenty of witty conversation.
255: Tomo-chan Is a Girl! by Fumita Yanagida (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Tomo Aizawa is a tough, sporty tomboy who's in love with her childhood friend Junichiro. The problem is that Jun has always seen her as one of the guys. Tomo is determined to make him see her as a girl, with plenty of help from her friends. It's a funny, sweet read for fans of short-chapter romance.
259: My Girlfriend's Child by Mamoru Aoi (Seven Seas) is a serious drama about teen pregnancy. A high school couple are very much in love, and after their first time together, the girl discovers she's pregnant. The two teens and their families must deal with the shock and the huge decisions that follow. It's an honest, emotional read for older teens and adults who like realistic stories.
260: Date A Live by Koushi Tachibana (Yen Press) is a romantic action comedy light novel. Spirits, powerful beings from another dimension, appear on Earth and cause disasters. Shido Itsuka, an ordinary high schooler, learns he has the unique ability to seal their powers, but only by making them fall in love with him. It's a funny, action-packed read for fans of harem comedies and sci-fi battles.
261: Reincarnated as a Dragon Hatchling by Necoco (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure. A man wakes up in another world reborn as a newly hatched dragon, alone in a forest full of dangerous monsters. Luckily, he can level up and evolve, and he sets out to grow stronger. It's an entertaining read for fans of monster-reincarnation stories.
263: Kodocha by Miho Obana (Tokyopop) is a shojo comedy. Sana Kurata is a bubbly child actress with a hit TV show and boundless energy. At school, though, her class is run by Akito Hayama, a troublemaker who makes the teachers miserable, so Sana decides to take him on. It's a funny, heartfelt classic that also deals with real family issues.
265: Detroit Metal City by Kiminori Wakasugi (Viz Media) is a seinen comedy. Soichi Negishi is a gentle young man who loves sweet pop music and dreams of singing it. Instead, he ends up as Johannes Krauser II, the frontman of an outrageous death metal band, and he's a huge hit. It's a hilarious, over-the-top read for fans of music and gross-out comedy.
266: Handyman Saitou in Another World by Katsumi Enami (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Saitou was a handyman back home who never felt appreciated for his work. After he's transported to a fantasy world, he joins a ragtag party of adventurers that needs exactly his kind of practical skills. It's a cozy, funny, and sometimes bittersweet read for those who enjoy found-family adventure stories.
268: Imitation by KyungRan Park (Yen Press) is a Korean drama romance. Lee Ma-ha is a member of a struggling K-pop girl group, nicknamed "Imitation" because she looks like a famous star. She works hard to make it, all while getting caught up with the members of a famous boy band. It's an inside look at the K-pop world for readers who enjoy music and showbiz romance.
269: Alice in Murderland by Kaori Yuki (Yen Press) is a dark gothic thriller. The wealthy Kuonji family holds a tea party every month, but this time, the mother makes an announcement: her children must fight each other to the death. Stella, the youngest, is pulled into a dangerous family game. It's a stylish read for fans of Kaori Yuki and twisted fairy-tale fantasy.
270: I'm the Evil Lord of an Intergalactic Empire! by Yomu Mishima (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi comedy light novel. Liam is reborn into a noble family in an interstellar empire, and he plans to live as a cruel, selfish lord. His idea of being "evil," though, keeps making him a great ruler, and his people love him for it. It's a funny read for those who enjoy misunderstandings and space opera.
271: From Far Away by Kyoko Hikawa (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy adventure. Noriko, an ordinary high school girl, is caught in an explosion and finds herself in a strange world. She's rescued by Izark, a quiet swordsman, and soon learns that she may be the "Awakening," a figure whose arrival is prophesied to bring disaster. It's a lovely fantasy romance for fans of classic shojo.
272: The Demon Sword Master of Excalibur Academy by Yu Shimizu (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Leonis Death Magnus, the Undead King, seals himself away to await a prophecy. When he awakens a thousand years later, he's in the body of a ten-year-old boy. Rescued by a girl named Riselia, he enrolls in a school that trains people to fight monsters. It's a fun read for fans of academy fantasy.
273: A Gentle Noble's Vacation Recommendation by Misaki (Yen Press) is a relaxed fantasy adventure. Lizel, a noble, ends up in another world with no idea how to get home. He decides to treat it as a vacation, hiring Gil, a powerful adventurer, as his guide and registering as an adventurer himself. It's a cozy, charming read for those who like slow-paced fantasy.
276: Tying the Knot with an Amagami Sister by Marcey Naito (Kodansha) is a romantic comedy. Uryu Kamihate is an orphan with big dreams of getting into a top medical school. He moves into a shrine run by three sisters, and the condition is that he marry one of them and take over the shrine. It's a fun, sweet read for fans of harem romance.
277: Kill Blue by Tadatoshi Fujimaki (Viz Media) is an action comedy. Juzo Ogami is a top assassin who gets stung by a strange wasp and finds himself back in the body of a junior high student. To find a cure, he has to go to school. It's a funny, action-packed read for fans of Fujimaki and school comedy.
282: See You in My 19th Life by Lee Hye (Ize Press) is a romantic drama. Ban Ji-eum remembers every one of her past lives. In her 19th life, she decides to find Mun Seo-ha, the boy she knew in her previous life. It's a heartfelt, beautiful romance for readers who love stories about fate and lasting love.
283: Steel Angel Kurumi by Kaishaku (ADV Manga) is a sci-fi comedy. Nakahito, a young boy, sneaks into a scientist's lab and accidentally awakens Kurumi, a powerful android girl built as a weapon, with a kiss. Kurumi is now completely devoted to him, much to his embarrassment. It's a silly, lighthearted read for those who enjoy android stories and slapstick comedy.
284: Suikoden III by Aki Shimizu (Tokyopop) is a fantasy war story based on the video game. In the Grasslands, war is brewing between the clans and their neighbors. Young Hugo of the Karaya clan crosses paths with Chris Lightfellow, a famous knight from the opposing side, and both are pulled into the conflict. It's a sweeping story for fans of the game and big fantasy adventures.
287: A Tropical Fish Yearns for Snow by Makoto Hagino (Viz Media) is a gentle yuri slice-of-life story. Konatsu moves from Tokyo to a small seaside town and struggles to fit in. There she meets Koyuki, the quiet, admired president of her school's aquarium club, who has her own reasons for keeping people at a distance. It's a soft, beautifully drawn read for fans of quiet romance.
289: Accel World by Hiroyuki Aigamo (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action manga based on the light novels by Reki Kawahara. Haruyuki Arita is a bullied boy who spends his time in virtual reality. Kuroyukihime, a beautiful student, introduces him to Brain Burst, a program that speeds up thought and turns him into a fighter. It's a solid pick for fans of Sword Art Online.
293: My Boy by Hitomi Takano (Vertical) is a josei drama. Satoko is a successful career woman whose life has taken a lonely turn. One night she meets Mashu, a quiet boy who is neglected at home, and the two begin to spend time together. It's a quiet, thoughtful read for adult readers who like complex relationships.
294: Akira by Katsuhiro Otomo (Kodansha) is a landmark cyberpunk sci-fi story. In Neo-Tokyo, decades after a mysterious explosion destroyed the old city, a teenage biker gang led by Kaneda runs into a secret government project. When Kaneda's friend Tetsuo begins to develop frightening psychic powers, the city starts to come apart. It's a classic for fans of sci-fi, action, and detailed artwork.
295: The Asterisk War by Yuu Miyazaki (Yen Press) is an action romance light novel. Ayato Amagiri transfers to Seidoukan Academy in Asterisk, a city where students fight in battles called Festas. On his first day, he accidentally sees Julis, a princess, changing, and she challenges him to a duel. It's a fun pick for fans of academy battle stories.
296: Golden Time by Yuyuko Takemiya (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Banri Tada has lost his memories in an accident and is starting over as a law student in Tokyo. On his first days of college, he meets Koko Kaga, a beautiful, intense girl with a dramatic entrance. It's a thoughtful, funny read for fans of college romance and the author's Toradora!
